source_roles.A: menjivar_2022_tps_contradictions (TPS survey + interview data on Salvadoran/Honduran holders)
source_roles.B: delreal_2022_venezuelan_legalization (extrapolated to US-TPS-Venezuelan context), fincen_2024_identity_fta, fincen_sar_key_terms, treasury_oig_fraud_alerts
source_roles.C: remitly_2024_10k (US→India/Mexico/Philippines corridor grounding), wise_2023_remittances_report (global sending-country context, hidden-fee awareness), iad_2026_remittance_year_in_review (LAC 2025 trends, remittance-tax policy, consolidation behaviour), oxfam_2018_central_america_myths (migration-driver context)
source_roles.D: no primary source; corridor + persona details are design assumptions

personas.name: Elena Reyes
personas.summary: Elena, 45, Salvadoran TPS holder. 20 years in the US, works as a hotel housekeeper in Los Angeles. Sends $300-400 monthly to her parents in San Miguel. Active in the local TPS Alliance committee. Every 18-month TPS-renewal cycle is an anxious reminder her life here is revocable. Has a US-born daughter in high school.

documentation_status.evidence_basis: Menjivar studies Salvadoran TPS holders; TPS = 'liminally legal, temporary and uncertain'

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Menjivar's core population; Oxfam Salvador 2015 homicide rate 103/100k as migration driver

income_pattern.evidence_basis: Menjivar: TPS holders do NOT derive significant occupational or earnings premium from higher education (Hypothesis 1-2.B supported)

civic_engagement.evidence_basis: Menjivar: National TPS Alliance formed 60+ committees after termination announcements; more educated TPS holders likelier to participate in community orgs

fraud_event_termination_anxiety.value: ambient vulnerability, not a specific fraud event
fraud_event_termination_anxiety.evidence_basis: Menjivar describes 'volatile climate' from TPS-termination announcements

name_and_biography.notes: design assumption — specific job role and city chosen to fit Menjivar's sample demography

personas.name: Carlos Mejía
personas.summary: Carlos, 38, Honduran TPS holder. 15 years in US, construction laborer in Houston. Sends $200-350 biweekly to his sister and two nephews in Tegucigalpa. Her husband was killed in gang violence in 2018. His high school education doesn't translate into better wages here — he earns the same as coworkers without it.

documentation_status.evidence_basis: Menjivar core population; Honduran TPS designated 1999, termination announced 2018

income_pattern.evidence_basis: Menjivar: no significant earnings premium for TPS holders

family_crisis_gang_violence.evidence_basis: Oxfam documents Central American gang violence as primary migration + transnational-family-concern driver

transfer_service_primary.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K names Honduras-equivalent LATAM corridors as core market; 5,100+ corridors served

personas.name: Ana Flores
personas.summary: Ana, 34, Venezuelan on TPS (designated March 2021). Miami home-health aide. Came via Colombia, spent 2 years in Bogotá on PEP before continuing to US. Sends $150-250 monthly to her father in Caracas through Zelle+family friend workaround. Monitoring news about TPS re-designation constantly.

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Del Real: 5.9M Venezuelans displaced; Colombia primary destination with 1.7M; onward migration to US documented

migration_driver.evidence_basis: Del Real: 'human rights violations, food shortages, violence, economic deterioration, and a crumbling healthcare system'

transit_via_colombia.evidence_basis: Del Real documents Colombian PEP for Venezuelan migrants; onward migration is known pattern

documentation_status.evidence_basis: Menjivar's liminal-legality framework extrapolates to Venezuelan TPS post-2021

name_and_biography.value: Ana Flores; Miami home-health; Caracas father

personas.name: Oluwaseun Okonkwo
personas.summary: Oluwaseun, 42, Nigerian, H-1B software engineer at a Sunnyvale startup since 2018. Sends $800-1,500 monthly to parents in Lagos, plus irregular larger amounts for his younger sister's Lagos tuition. Uses Remitly app for speed + Sendwave for rate comparison. Tech-savvy; price-aware.

transfer_service_primary.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: 5,100+ corridors, Nigeria is a major African receive market; mobile-app primary

fee_awareness.evidence_basis: Wise: McKinsey finds 50% of cross-border payment fees are FX margin; awareness correlates with H-1B tech workers

fraud_exposure_whatsapp.evidence_basis: FinCEN SAR key terms include BEC fraud; impersonation via messaging apps is a documented typology (SAR_ADVISORY_BEC_FRAUD)

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Remitly names 170+ countries served, Africa is listed in largest disbursement regions

personas.name: Priya Sharma
personas.summary: Priya, 29, Indian H-1B engineer at Microsoft in Seattle. Sends $1,000-2,000 monthly to her parents in Mumbai via Remitly. Uses the app's rate-alerts feature. Her dad is retired, her mom runs a small sari shop. Monitors INR-USD rate daily.

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: India named among 'largest receive countries'; high-average-send-amount corridor

transfer_service_primary.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: India is one of its top three receive markets; mobile-app primary engagement

fee_awareness.evidence_basis: Wise: G20 remittance report frames fee awareness as key variable; tech-worker profile correlates

fraud_exposure_tech_support.evidence_basis: FinCEN FTA T10 (Scam) covers impersonation-based schemes targeting specific demographics

personas.name: Maria Garcia
personas.summary: Maria, 52, Mexican-born legal permanent resident. Domestic worker in San Diego for 25 years. Sends $200-300 biweekly to her widowed mother and two siblings in a small Michoacán town via Western Union in-person at a Mexican-owned bodega. Doesn't trust apps. Cash deposits only. Faced 1% remittance tax (Big Beautiful Bill 2025) that now costs her $4/transfer.

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: Mexico is a top-three receive market

transfer_service_primary.evidence_basis: IAD 2026: ~45% of senders use agent locations; 45% remit in cash; WU acquiring Intermex gives ~30% market share

remittance_tax_impact.evidence_basis: IAD 2026: Big Beautiful Bill 2025 1% remittance tax; affects 50%+ of senders; est $4 per-transaction cost

mexico_corridor_decline.evidence_basis: IAD 2026: Mexico the only LAC negative performer in 2025; 4% of remitters ceased sending

fraud_exposure_ice_call.evidence_basis: Treasury OIG: documented IRS/government-impersonation scheme targeting US populations

name_and_biography.value: Maria Garcia; San Diego domestic worker; Michoacán family

personas.name: Raymart Cruz
personas.summary: Raymart, 35, Filipino-born, nurse at a Dallas hospital, on a 2nd-cycle H-1B. Sends $500-800 twice monthly to his wife and three kids in Cebu. Uses Remitly app almost exclusively. Pays Philippine SSS and PhilHealth premiums for parents back home.

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: Philippines is a top-three receive country

sender_demographics.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: 'immigrants and other global citizens' primary customer; US→Philippines large corridor

name_and_biography.value: Raymart Cruz; Dallas hospital; Cebu family

personas.name: Yosef Tesfaye
personas.summary: Yosef, 27, Ethiopian asylee, Uber/Lyft driver in DC for 3 years. Was targeted by a phone scam in 2024 claiming to be from the IRS demanding back taxes; he nearly wired $1,200 via Green Dot before a friend intervened. Sends $100-200 monthly to his mother in Addis Ababa via Sendwave.

fraud_exposure_primary.evidence_basis: Treasury OIG documents ongoing IRS/Treasury-impersonation scheme demanding payment; FinCEN FTA T10 (Scam) covers

near_miss_payment_method.evidence_basis: FTC Sentinel + Treasury OIG: prepaid-card payment is a top imposter-scam payment method

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Design choice — no specific source grounds Ethiopia corridor

name_and_biography.value: Yosef Tesfaye; DC ride-share; 2024 near-miss scam

personas.name: Kwame Mensah
personas.summary: Kwame, 45, Ghanaian-born naturalized US citizen, NYC taxi driver for 18 years. Married with two daughters at Howard & Rutgers. Sends $400-600 monthly to his mother and sisters in Accra. Uses a mix of Western Union (when he doesn't trust the latest Wise rate) and a cousin-run informal network that routes via Ghanaian merchants in the Bronx. Aware FX markups are hidden.

transfer_service_loyalty.secondary: informal Ghanaian merchant network + Wise app

fee_awareness.evidence_basis: Wise 2023 + Canada data: only 20% of consumers can identify FX markups, but long-tenure senders often do

informal_channel_usage.value: partial — cousin network via Bronx Ghanaian merchants
informal_channel_usage.evidence_basis: FinCEN SAR_ADVISORY_IVTS covers informal value transfer systems; common in African diaspora

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Remitly 10-K: 170+ countries, Africa core region, Ghana a documented corridor

name_and_biography.value: Kwame Mensah; NYC taxi; Accra family

personas.name: Ricardo Domínguez
personas.summary: Ricardo, 55, Dominican-born, long-time Bronx resident, US citizen since 2009. Grocery-store manager. Sends $300-400 monthly to cousins in Santo Domingo and a nephew in La Vega. Uses Walmart-to-Walmart for predictable flat pricing. His wife handles the family's savings.

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Design — no v3 source directly grounds DR corridor

all_fields.notes: Grade D — no source grounds this persona's core fields

personas.name: Carmen Pérez
personas.summary: Carmen, 62, Puerto Rican (mainland-US resident since 1998), Brooklyn. Home health aide, union member. Was targeted by a grandparent-impersonation scam in 2024 — a caller pretending to be her grandson claimed he was in jail and needed bail wired. She caught it because he called her 'abuelita' but her actual grandson calls her 'mami.' Sends $150-250 monthly to her elderly mother in Ponce (domestic-but-remittance-category flows).
personas.corridor_country: Puerto Rico (Ponce) — domestic US but remittance-pattern

fraud_exposure_grandparent_scam.evidence_basis: SAR_ADVISORY_ELDER_FINANCIAL_EXPLOITATION (FIN-2022-A002); 'grandparent scam' is canonical elder-exploitation imposter scheme

elder_vulnerability.evidence_basis: FinCEN Elder Financial Exploitation advisory covers age 60+

name_and_biography.notes: fraud-vector-defined persona; detection detail ('abuelita' tell) is design

personas.name: Aleksandr Petrov
personas.summary: Aleksandr, 48, Russian-born naturalized US citizen, software consultant in Austin. Sends $500-1,500 occasionally to his adult daughter studying in Almaty, Kazakhstan, and to an aging aunt in Yekaterinburg. Uses Wise for the rate; Russian-banking sanctions make the Russia side tricky. Monitors routing carefully.

transfer_service_loyalty.secondary: (routed via intermediary banks due to sanctions)

corridor_country.evidence_basis: Design — Wise report explicitly excludes Russia due to sanctions; no v3 source grounds these corridors

all_fields.notes: Grade D — deliberately included to provide corridor diversity outside the sourced set
